text:
sam_sales: FYI kickoff for ACME hybrid POC. They want Private deployment in our AWS account via PrivateLink, but they also have an on‑prem edge that needs source IP preservation and optional TLS inspection. Need architecture + firewall/EIP guidance + pricing sketch.

alex_solutions: Copy — can you paste the customer network constraints (NAT, TLS inspect box, BGP?) and the timeline?

sam_sales: Notes from call: customer runs Palo Alto at colo, wants to terminate TLS for DLP at their side. They have BGP to colo and can peer with TGW, but security prefers PrivateLink for isolation. Timeline: 2‑week POC, then 8‑12 week prod.

maria_netops: Quick reality check: PrivateLink endpoints are ENIs in customer VPC — traffic originates from our PrivateLink service NLB in our VPC. If they need original client source IP at their on‑prem inspected box, we'll need to preserve IP via a transit setup (e.g., TGW with proxy or BYO IP on the connector). PrivateLink alone will NAT to the endpoint IPs.

devon_se: For the POC, two pragmatic options:
- Option A (simpler): PrivateLink + small NAT pool (static EIPs) we advertise. Customer accepts SNAT so their TLS box sees our EIP as client.
- Option B (preserve src IP): Transit (TGW) + proxy appliance in their VPC forwarding to on‑prem via VPN/DirectConnect; we may need to run NATless connector and coordinate BGP. More setup/time.

jess_security: Security checklist items from compliance team: KMS integration for keys, HSM option for enterprise, audit logs retained 90d, TLS cipher policy, and app-level token redaction. Also need answers for standard questionnaire Q12 (are any customer IPs stored on Redwood infra?).

sam_sales: Customer asked about cost impact of static EIPs and Dedicated capacity for predictable latency. Any rough numbers for the POC?

alex_solutions: POC sketch: Dedicated reserved capacity adds predictable throughput (example: small reserved pool ~$8k/mo) — we can give an internal ballpark but final depends on qps/seq len. Static EIP provisioning: AWS charges + management; our ops cost to reserve and attach per‑POC is typically a small one‑time setup fee. For sales, say: "reserved capacity + 2 static EIPs" estimate, then we'll refine.

maria_netops: Also call out limits: PrivateLink has ENI scale and concurrent connections per NLB target. If customer wants high parallelism, TGW/Shared infra may be better. For POC (low qps), PrivateLink fine.

sam_sales: Customer security questionnaire also asks for firewall rule examples to put in their Palo Alto. Can we provide minimal allowlist for POC?

alex_solutions: Minimal inbound rules (on customer side toward our PrivateLink ENI):
```
- Allow TCP 443 from customer-subnet(s) -> interface-endpoint ENIs
- Allow established/related return traffic
- ICMP (optional) for health checks
```
If using NAT/EIP egress from our side to onprem TLS box: customer should allow our static EIP(s) on port 443.

maria_netops: Example ACL for their edge (palo):
```
rule allow_redwood_poc {
  source: 10.10.0.0/16  # their app subnets
  dest: 3.120.45.0/24   # our POC egress pool (example)
  proto: tcp
  ports: 443
  action: allow
}
```
I'll mark the dest CIDR as placeholder — we'll provide the exact CIDR once infra team allocates EIPs.

jess_security: Also provide the questionnaire snippet re: data residency: "All inference request logs stored in customer‑scoped audit log with retention policy X; any PII redaction occurs before long‑term storage." I'll draft exact wording to satisfy legal.

sam_sales: Blockers: procurement needs vendor security attestation (SOC2) and a simple runbook for incident escalation. Can infra/bizops supply?

infra-bot: deploy_job:privatedeploy-poc-3312345678 initiated by devon_se at 3312345700 — provisioning footprint: 2x EIP placeholders, 1x small reserved pool. ETA config artifacts 03h.

devon_se: I'll coordinate the reserved pool + EIP allocation. Maria — can you confirm whether we can announce the EIPs to customer via their BGP if we do Option B?

maria_netops: Yes, we can announce via a temporary BGP session on the colo edge, but that requires approvals and a change window. For the 2‑week POC we usually avoid full BGP unless customer insists.

sam_sales: Action items: 1) devon: produce rough cost breakdown for reserved capacity + 2 static EIPs by EOD. 2) alex: draft minimal firewall snippet + questionnaire answers. 3) jess: SOC2 attestation + incident runbook stub. 4) maria: confirm if we can do BGP announce in a 48h change window. I'll send customer a one‑pager after we have these.

alex_solutions: Ack — will drop the firewall snippet + questionnaire answers into the POC folder and ping when ready. Link: https://redwood.internal/poc/acme/3312345678 (placeholder). :thumbsup:

sam_sales: Thanks team — keeping this thread for POC comms. If anything slips, escalate to #eng‑sre.

devon_se: updated cost sketch posted in doc; ping me if you want numbers adjusted for 250 qps.

jess_security: Draft questionnaire ready for review, pushed to the doc. I'll also attach the KMS/HSM config options.

sam_sales: closing loop — customer call scheduled tomorrow 09:00 PT, please have at least one SME on call.
